ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The signal-flow graph in the attachment has U(s) as the input and C(s) as the output from left to right. On the main path there are two integrator blocks labeled 1/s; the input U(s) first passes through the forward gain h0 into the left summing node, and then passes through the first 1/s; the output of the first integrator goes to the second summing node and then passes through the second 1/s to the output C(s). There is also an upper feedforward branch in the figure, labeled h1, bridging from the input side to the second summing node. Below there are two feedback branches: one labeled -a1 feeds back from the output of the first integrator to the left summing node; the other labeled -a0 feeds back from the output side to the left summing node. Then reasoning: Let the output of the first integrator be x(s), and the output of the second integrator be y(s)=C(s). The input to the left summing node is h0 U(s)-a1 x(s)-a0 y(s), and x(s) is obtained by passing that node signal through 1/s, so s x(s)=h0 U(s)-a1 x(s)-a0 y(s). The summing node before the second integrator receives x(s) and the upper feedforward h1 U(s), so s y(s)=x(s)+h1 U(s). From the second equation, x(s)=s y(s)-h1 U(s). Substitute into the first equation: s[s y(s)-h1 U(s)]=h0 U(s)-a1[s y(s)-h1 U(s)]-a0 y(s). Arranging gives (s^2+a1 s+a0)y(s)=(h1 s+h0+a1 h1)U(s). Therefore G(s)=C(s)/U(s)=(h1 s+h0+a1 h1)/(s^2+a1 s+a0). Substituting h1=b1, h0=b0-b1 a1, the numerator becomes b1 s+(b0-b1 a1)+a1 b1=b1 s+b0, so G(s)=(b1 s+b0)/(s^2+a1 s+a0).

raw_record.original_question: The signal flow graph of a system is shown below. \(U(s)\) is the input and \(C(s)\) is the output. Assuming \(h_1=b_1\) and \(h_0=b_0-b_1a_1\), what is the input-output transfer function \(G(s)=\frac{C(s)}{U(s)}\) of the system?
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: The signal-flow graph in the attachment has U(s) as the input and C(s) as the output from left to right. On the main path there are two integrator blocks labeled 1/s; the input U(s) first passes through the forward gain h0 into the left summing node, and then passes through the first 1/s; the output of the first integrator goes to the second summing node and then passes through the second 1/s to the output C(s). There is also an upper feedforward branch in the figure, labeled h1, bridging from the input side to the second summing node. Below there are two feedback branches: one labeled -a1 feeds back from the output of the first integrator to the left summing node; the other labeled -a0 feeds back from the output side to the left summing node. Then reasoning: Let the output of the first integrator be x(s), and the output of the second integrator be y(s)=C(s). The input to the left summing node is h0 U(s)-a1 x(s)-a0 y(s), and x(s) is obtained by passing that node signal through 1/s, so s x(s)=h0 U(s)-a1 x(s)-a0 y(s). The summing node before the second integrator receives x(s) and the upper feedforward h1 U(s), so s y(s)=x(s)+h1 U(s). From the second equation, x(s)=s y(s)-h1 U(s). Substitute into the first equation: s[s y(s)-h1 U(s)]=h0 U(s)-a1[s y(s)-h1 U(s)]-a0 y(s). Arranging gives (s^2+a1 s+a0)y(s)=(h1 s+h0+a1 h1)U(s). Therefore G(s)=C(s)/U(s)=(h1 s+h0+a1 h1)/(s^2+a1 s+a0). Substituting h1=b1, h0=b0-b1 a1, the numerator becomes b1 s+(b0-b1 a1)+a1 b1=b1 s+b0, so G(s)=(b1 s+b0)/(s^2+a1 s+a0).
